independent.title: 独立マーチャント（四方モード）

independent.desc: 四方直接清算モードでは、FilixPayが決済ゲートウェイとして機能し、取引を提携のライセンス取得済みアクワイアラへルーティングして精算します。資金は中間口座を経由せず、直接あなたの銀行口座に入金されます。

sub_merchant.title: サブマーチャント（三方モード）
sub_merchant.slogan: FilixPay（またはグループインスタンス）が集金し、その後あなたへ精算

features.title: オールインワン集約決済 – 主要グローバルチャネルとのシームレスな統合
features.subtitle: FilixPayマーチャントセンターを通じて、Alipay、WeChat Pay、PayPal、Stripe、NowPaymentsなど、複数の決済チャネルを簡単に設定できます。ローカルでも国際的でも、一度の統合で全ての決済方法を一元的に管理できます。

unified.title: 独立デプロイ可能なチェックアウト

features.title: クラスタ対応、弾力的な拡張性

trusted_ledger.title: 次のコア能力：グローバル信頼台帳エンジン

key_value.title: 核心価値：チェーンのサイロを打破し、統一された信頼レイヤーを構築

items.title: マルチチェーン対応、主流エコシステムへワンクリック接続
items.desc: ChainMaker、FISCO BCOS、AntChainなどの主要コンソーシアムブロックチェーンプラットフォームとネイティブに深く統合し、標準化されたアクセスキットを提供。統一抽象レイヤーにより、企業が複数のブロックチェーンネットワークへ接続・管理する複雑さと技術的ハードルを低減し、「一度開発、複数チェーンへ展開」を実現します。

items.title: クロスチェーン信頼、エコシステム連携価値を活性化
items.desc: 企業が異なるブロックチェーン上に事業を構築している現実を踏まえ、本エンジンはコンプライアンスの枠組み内で、重要ビジネスデータや資産証明を異種チェーン間で安全かつ信頼できる形で流通・検証できます。行政チェーン上の政府承認、金融チェーン上の証明、サプライチェーン上の注文が相互にアンカー・参照し合い、クロスドメイン・クロス機関の信頼連携ネットワークを構築します。

items.title: コンプライアントな相互運用、規制と自律の要件に対応
items.desc: すべてのクロスチェーン連携設計は、国内のデータセキュリティおよび業界規制基準に厳密に従い、流通プロセス全体の監査可能性と追跡可能性を確保します。国家・業界レベルのブロックチェーンインフラ（「スパークチェーンネットワーク」など）との統合をサポートし、デジタル経済のより広範な信頼エコシステムに参加します。

scenarios.title: 活用シナリオ：散在する信頼の島をつなぐ

items.title: クロスドメイン・サプライチェーンファイナンス
items.desc: コア企業が属するサプライチェーン、銀行が運用する金融チェーン、港湾の物流チェーンをつなぎ、財産権・債権・キャッシュフローのマルチチェーン同期と自動清算を実現します。

items.title: 地域政府サービスの統合
items.desc: 省・部門ごとに異なるブロックチェーン上に構築された政府システムを橋渡しし、企業や市民が「オンチェーンでの省をまたいだサービス」の利便性を享受できるようにします。

items.desc: 異なる技術路線を用いる業界アライアンス内の加盟企業が、既存システムを改修することなく、重要な生産データ、カーボンフットプリント、品質トレーサビリティ情報の信頼できる相互認識を実現できるよう支援します。

items.title: 1. WeChat Pay: Fund Freezing & Unfreezing Model
items.desc: WeChat's splitting mechanism centers on 'Freeze First, Split Later,' ideal for scenarios requiring delayed splitting or with refund risks.

flow.title: Core Workflow:
steps: Transaction & Freezing: Upon successful payment, funds are frozen in the merchant's account (Pending Split state) instead of entering available balance.
Initiate Split: When split conditions are met (e.g., delivery confirmed), the split API is called. WeChat unfreezes and allocates funds to specified receivers.
Complete Split: If no further splitting is needed, the completion API unfreezes remaining funds to the merchant's available balance.

compliance.title: Key Compliance Points:
items: Split Ratio Limit: Default maximum is usually 30% of the order amount (adjustable with authorization).
Split Duration: Funds can be frozen for up to 180 days (some docs mention 30 days; auto-unfreeze occurs if no split is initiated).
Split Frequency: Supports multiple splits (up to 50 times) to multiple parties (up to 50 receivers per split).

items.title: 2. Alipay: Settlement Confirmation & Asynchronous Splitting
items.desc: Alipay emphasizes 'Settlement Confirmation' and offers strong synch/asynch capabilities for high-concurrency scenarios.

flow.title: Core Workflow:
steps: Transaction & Freezing: Funds enter a pending settlement state. The platform initiates 'Confirm Settlement' to freeze funds for splitting.
Initiate Split: Calling the settlement API (alipay.trade.order.settle) supports both synchronous (real-time) and asynchronous (high-frequency) modes.
Reverse Split: Supports original-path reversal of split funds in case of refunds.

compliance.title: Key Compliance Points:
items: Split Ratio Limit: Maximum amount cannot exceed 100% of the order total plus supplements (policy dependent).
Split Validity: Splitting is typically valid for up to 365 days after the transaction.
Receiver Binding: Receivers must be real-name verified and added to the platform's 'Split Relation Set' via API.
Performance: Sync mode is limited (30 QPS), while async mode supports up to 500 QPS for high-traffic platforms.

items.title: 3. Stripe: Separate Charges and Transfers (Connect)
items.desc: Stripe Connect is highly flexible, using the 'Separate Charges and Transfers' model for complex global or multi-party marketplaces.

flow.title: Core Workflow:
steps: Platform Collection: A PaymentIntent is created on the platform's Stripe account; funds initially belong to the platform.
Trigger Transfer: Upon success, the platform calls the Transfers API (often triggered by payment_intent.succeeded webhooks).
Fund Allocation: Transfers are linked to origin charges via source_transaction, allowing funds to flow automatically to Connected Accounts during settlement.

compliance.title: Key Compliance Points:
items: Insufficient Balance: source_transaction linking avoids transfer failures due to lack of platform balance by processing via internal fund flows.
Application Fees: Platforms can deduct service fees (application_fee_amount) at collection before distributing the remainder.
Flexibility: Supports splitting to multiple receivers (sellers, affiliates, logistics) without fixed ratio constraints (subject to platform agreement).

pain_points.title: Fund Control Gaps in Group Operations

items.title: Personal QR Code Collection
items.desc: Stores and project teams accept payments via personal WeChat or Alipay accounts, bypassing group accounts so headquarters cannot track inflows in real time.
items.consequences: Off-book fund loops, reconciliation pain, distorted operating data.

items.title: Third-Party Account Diversion
items.desc: Business receipts flow into third-party platforms or personal accounts outside group control, creating off-book pools and weakening centralized fund scheduling.
items.consequences: Fragmented funds, compliance exposure, decisions without reliable data.

items.title: Fragmented Payment Channels
items.desc: Each legal entity connects to payment providers independently with different rates and settlement cycles, making reconciliation error-prone and costly.
items.consequences: Unreliable reporting, high maintenance, complex integrations.

items.title: Off-Book Fund Pools
items.desc: Some revenue never reaches governed accounts or moves through informal channels, so the group cannot see true operating and fund positions.
items.consequences: Weak internal controls, costly audits, low fund transparency.

rules.title: Core Business Rules
items: Governance Boundary
Enterprise governs at the group level (creating and managing Organizations). It does not directly own, control, or suspend Merchants — authorization stays within each Organization.
Unified Collection
The group may set unified acquiring policies; each Organization signs and operates under its legal entity.
Fund Collection
Customer payments flow into supervised accounts — external collection channels and personal QR codes are prohibited.
Split Settlement
Licensed split APIs automate clearing and reduce manual fund transit risk.
Approval Workflow
Cross-organization fund movements require group approval before execution.

identity.title: Identity & Auth
identity.hero_title: Enterprise Identity: Building a Financial-Grade Security Foundation with Keycloak
identity.hero_desc: In payment systems, identity authentication is not only the first door of user experience but also the core defense line for fund security and compliant operations. We adopt Keycloak - an open-source Identity and Access Management (IAM) platform led by Red Hat - as a unified identity authentication engine, providing financial-grade security, global compliance support, and capacity for tens of millions of users for your payment business.
identity.why_keycloak_title: ✅ Why Keycloak? — Verified by Top Global Institutions
identity.why_keycloak_desc: Keycloak has been deeply adopted by numerous industries with high security requirements, including finance, government, telecommunications, and cloud computing:

cases.name: Hitachi
cases.desc: Built an authorization server for Japanese banks that meets Financial-grade API (FAPI) standards, passing 700+ consistency tests to meet the most stringent open banking compliance requirements.

cases.name: Austrian Federal Computing Centre (BRZ)
cases.desc: As a technology partner of the Austrian government, it supports unified authentication for 2 million+ users and 130+ public services, operating stably for many years.

cases.name: Infosys
cases.desc: Built an identity platform for a large Japanese pharmaceutical group, managing over 2 million users and supporting 4000+ pharmacists logging in safely daily in 750+ pharmacies.

cases.name: VMware (Broadcom)
cases.desc: Deeply integrated Keycloak into its Telco Cloud Operations platform to achieve automated management of users, roles, and permissions.

identity.cases_conclusion: These cases prove: Keycloak can not only handle high concurrency and large-scale user pressure but also meet the compliance thresholds of highly regulated industries such as finance and government.
identity.features_title: 🔐 Security Capabilities Tailored for Payment Scenarios
identity.feature_1_desc: Full implementation of OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0; native support for FAPI (Financial-grade API) security specifications to meet PSD2 and open banking compliance; support for PKCE, MTLS, JWT signature verification, and other advanced security mechanisms.
identity.feature_2_desc: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): SMS, TOTP, WebAuthn (FIDO2); Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and fine-grained permission policies; session management: automatic timeout, forced logout, and device binding.
identity.feature_3_desc: GDPR Ready: Data minimization, consent management, data export/deletion; PCI DSS Friendly: No contact with cardholder data (PAN), serves only as an authentication layer, reducing compliance scope; compatible with multi-level protection scheme (MLPS) requirements.
identity.feature_4_desc: Supports cluster deployment, database sharding, and cache optimization; proven in multiple national platforms to handle millions of daily active users; private deployment ensures data sovereignty and network isolation.

identity.integration_desc: Keycloak provides standardized interfaces for easy integration with:
identity.integration_footer: Also supports federation with existing identity sources like LDAP, Active Directory, and social accounts for a smooth migration without burden.
